A low starting organic fraction should retain and separate the early pair, while 40 C tests improved selectivity for the pairs crowded at 25 C. This intermediate gradient slope should spread the middle peaks more than injection 8 while the higher endpoint brings the last compound out near 10 minutes.

Lengthen only the gradient to test whether the sole under-resolved pair responds to a shallower slope. The 1.16-minute margin below the time-penalty threshold should accommodate this modest increase while potentially bringing its resolution to 1.5.

Raise temperature by one step while retaining the fully resolving gradient to move the last peak clearly below 10 minutes. This isolates the temperature effect on selectivity, especially whether the critical pair retains R ≥ 1.5.

Return to 40 C and use a gradient slope between injections 9 and 10, closer to the fully resolved method. This should preserve R ≥ 1.5 for the critical pair while bringing the last peak below 10 minutes; the 0.65 endpoint remains above its estimated elution fraction.

Keep injection 12 as the maximum-score benchmark and test a shorter separation at 55 C. The critical pair converged from 40 to 45 C, so this larger temperature shift tests whether it crosses and separates again while the last peak elutes earlier.

Shorten the fully resolving 55 C gradient by one grid step to seek an earlier last peak while preserving the maximum CRF. Holding temperature and endpoints fixed isolates the slope response, especially for the two closest pairs.

Narrow the organic window to give a slope between injections 13 and 14, aiming to restore the newly critical pair to R ≥ 1.5 while retaining the other pair’s resolution. The last peak should remain within the gradient and elute earlier than in injection 13.

Shift the gradient window upward while preserving injection 15’s slope to seek a shorter fully resolved separation. The early pair has substantial resolution margin, but the two critical middle pairs will determine whether the higher starting organic fraction is acceptable.

Lower the starting organic fraction to improve the pair that deteriorated when phi0 increased, while using a steeper slope than injection 15 to shorten late retention. This tests whether both critical pairs can remain fully resolved with the last peak earlier than 8 minutes.

Increase the endpoint by one step to test the speed limit around injection 17, the shortest fully resolved method so far. Both critical pairs have little resolution margin, so this run will establish whether further gradient steepening is acceptable.

With maximum-CRF methods secured, test a faster selectivity regime at 60 C with a steeper gradient. The critical middle pair may cross and separate in reversed order, potentially allowing a substantially shorter fully resolved run.

Increase only the gradient slope to test whether the remaining close pair separates further in the apparent reversed-order regime. Monitor the neighboring pair at R 1.62, which may become limiting as the run shortens.

The close pair responds weakly to slope, so test a higher starting organic fraction to shift its selectivity, with a slightly shallower gradient to protect its neighbor. The early pair may become limiting; retain injection 17 as the shortest fully resolved benchmark.

Return to the fully resolving 55 C regime with a slope between injections 14 and 15. This targets full resolution of both critical pairs with a last peak slightly earlier than injection 15, avoiding the selectivity losses seen at 60 C.

Slightly flatten injection 22’s gradient to increase the limiting pair’s resolution margin while keeping the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes. This targets a more robust maximum-score method, with injection 17 retained as the shortest fully resolved option.

Lengthen injection 16’s gradient to recover its sole under-resolved pair while exploiting the improved separation of the other critical pair at phi0 0.15. This targets a maximum-score method with greater resolution margin and a last peak still below 10 minutes.
